business_objective: Replace lost or damaged event badges for active registrations and close each request after replacement collection is acknowledged.

stakeholder_statements.text: An attendee submits a badge-replacement request and identifies the registration and replacement reason.
The registration clerk confirms that the registration is active.
The badge desk officer records the old badge as lost or damaged and invalidates it.
After active registration is confirmed, the credential issuer records the replacement badge as issued. The attendee acknowledges collection of the replacement badge.

The event access supervisor closes the replacement request only after the old badge is invalidated and collection is acknowledged. Registration transfer and ticket refund processing are outside this project.

business_objective: Review service-fee waiver requests and apply approved waivers after hardship eligibility and finance approval are recorded.

stakeholder_statements.text: A resident submits a service-fee waiver request and identifies the service application and reason for requesting relief.
The service intake clerk records the supporting evidence and hardship category. The accepted evidence types and hardship categories have not been agreed.
The eligibility officer records the request as eligible or ineligible and adds a rationale when it is ineligible. The eligibility criteria are undecided.
The finance reviewer records the waiver as approved or returned. The finance-approval criteria are not finalized.

The service records clerk applies the waiver only after eligibility and finance approval are recorded. The clerk sends the outcome to the resident, but the delivery channel is undecided. Refunding paid fees and changing the underlying service decision are outside this project.

business_objective: Review learner appeals about activity-completion status and update completion records when an appeal is upheld.

stakeholder_statements.text: A learner submits a completion-status appeal and identifies the course activity and disputed completion status.
The learning support clerk records the supporting evidence and appeal-reason category. The accepted evidence types and reason categories have not been agreed.
The instructor records whether the activity requirements were met and adds an explanation. The evaluation criteria are not finalized.
The academic reviewer records the appeal as upheld or declined after reviewing the instructor finding. The appeal-decision criteria are undecided.

The completion records officer updates the completion status only for an upheld appeal and sends the outcome to the learner. The delivery channel is undecided. Grade changes and certificate issuance are outside this project.

business_objective: Verify employee qualifications and publish confirmed qualifications to workforce profiles using a recorded visibility designation.

stakeholder_statements.text: An employee submits a qualification-verification request and identifies the qualification and issuing body.
The HR records clerk records the completion date and supporting evidence. The accepted evidence types have not been agreed.
The credential reviewer records the qualification as authentic or not authentic and adds a rationale when it is not authentic. The verification criteria are undecided.
The workforce profile curator records the qualification category and visibility designation. The category and visibility options are not finalized.

The HR profile officer publishes the qualification to the employee profile only after authenticity is confirmed and a visibility designation is recorded, then sends the outcome to the employee. The delivery channel is undecided. Recruitment decisions and salary changes are outside this project.

business_objective: Review workspace compliance-export requests while preserving an unresolved rule about disclosure of former-member identities.

stakeholder_statements.text: A workspace owner submits a compliance-export request and identifies the workspace and requested data categories.
The data export specialist records the export period and the data categories included in the export package.
The audit lead records an audit-purpose note. The audit lead says former-member names must remain visible so the export preserves the original audit trail.
The privacy reviewer records a disclosure assessment and required redactions. The reviewer says former-member names must be masked unless those members consent.

The workspace governance officer records an approved or declined release decision after the export scope, audit-purpose note, privacy assessment, and required redactions are present. Nobody has decided who resolves the identity-visibility disagreement, what evidence proves former-member consent, which data categories require redaction, or the maximum review time. Permanent workspace deletion and subscription billing are outside this project; the meeting also wandered into complaints about the conference-room carpet.
